summary: Igloolik Airport is a small regional airport serving the Inuit hamlet of Igloolik on a small island in Foxe Basin, Nunavut, in the Canadian Arctic. Situated well above the Arctic Circle at roughly 69 degrees north latitude, it serves as a critical lifeline for a remote community of approximately 1,700 people. The airport primarily handles turboprop aircraft on routes connecting to other Nunavut communities and southern Canada.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Igloolik Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by Calm Air and Canadian North, which operate turboprop flights connecting Igloolik to other Nunavut communities like Iqaluit and Hall Beach, as well as to Winnipeg in Manitoba.

Q: Does Igloolik Airport have any road connections?
A: No, there are no roads connecting Igloolik to other communities. Travel to and from the airport is exclusively by air, or seasonally by sea when the waters of Foxe Basin allow boat access.

Q: How long is the runway at Igloolik Airport?
A: The airport features a single gravel runway approximately 3,800 feet long, suitable for turboprop aircraft common in Arctic operations.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Igloolik?
A: The airport operates year-round, but summer months (June through August) typically offer more reliable weather conditions and longer daylight hours for travel.
transport_tips: There are no public bus services or taxi ranks at Igloolik Airport; passengers typically arrange ground transportation in advance with local contacts, hotels, or by contacting the airline before arrival. The airport is located just a few kilometers from the hamlet center, so pre-arranged pickup is straightforward. Rental cars are not available locally, so most visitors rely on accommodation hosts or community contacts for transportation.
